ov: The lesser apes: about 20 species of tailless apes of Asian forests. They swing arm over arm (brachiation) up to 15 m at a time at up to 55 km/h, and mated pairs sing duets that can carry 1 km.

why.d: About 60% of the diet is fruit, with leaves and twigs, but they also eat some insects and occasionally birds’ eggs.
why.et: Sometimes hunted by villagers for food.

rg: Subtropical and tropical forests from eastern Bangladesh and Northeast India to Southeast Asia, Sumatra, Borneo and Java.
df: About 60% fruit, plus twigs, leaves, insects, flowers and occasionally birds’ eggs.
fx: Gibbons can leap up to 8 m.
Pairs usually keep the same mate for life, though they sometimes "divorce".

_cf.tip: A gibbon is a small ape, not a monkey. Like all apes it has no tail, and it swings arm over arm between branches.
